prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1108; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: The insured reported a left-turn collision at an intersection and said the other vehicle struck the passenger side of her car as it crossed the oncoming lane. She is reporting neck and back strain and has retained counsel, so all contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: The driver is named on the policy and the vehicle is listed as a covered unit. Nothing in our records suggests the damage occurred before coverage began.

Entry 3: Photos taken at the scene show damage that lines up with the described impact on the passenger side and front quarter panel. The estimate has been sent to the appraiser for review.

Entry 4: Police and two drivers at the scene confirm the claimant was in the vehicle at the time. No independent witnesses have come forward to describe how the collision happened.

Entry 5: The claimant's account of the crash has stayed consistent across the recorded statement, the follow-up call, and the written summary from counsel. The details of the turn and the point of impact match each time.

Entry 6: Medical records show a neck and back strain, which is a plausible injury for a side impact of this type. No earlier injury to the same body area appears in the claim history or prior records we obtained.

Entry 7: Treatment began within a few days of the collision and followed a typical course of physical therapy and medication. Visits tapered off as her range of motion improved and her pain eased.

Entry 8: The appraiser reviewed the vehicle and found no earlier damage to the same panels. The repair scope fits the impact pattern described in the statement and the scene photos.

Entry 9: Counsel has asked for a settlement of the bodily injury portion of the claim. The request is being reviewed against the treatment records and the billing summary.

Entry 10: The bills received so far are itemized and match the treatment dates in the medical file. The adjuster will complete the evaluation of the injury claim once the final records arrive.

Entry 11: File reviewed and current status recorded. Property damage is ready for payment on the repair estimate, and the bodily injury evaluation remains open pending the final medical summary.
